questions.question: There are main types of cell division in humans.
questions.questionHtml: There are <u>      </u> main types of cell division in humans.
questions.solution: Cell division is the process by which a parent cell divides into two or more daughter cells. There are two types of cell division: mitosis and meiosis. Mitosis creates new body cells, while meiosis creates egg and sperm cells. Mitosis is seen in somatic cells of animals and produces two genetically identical daughter cells.

questions.question: The transportation mechanism in cells by which food or other useful molecules from the outside are carried inside the cell is known as ____________.
questions.questionHtml: The transportation mechanism in cells by which food or other useful molecules from the outside are carried inside the cell is known as ____________.
questions.solution: Endocytosis is the process by which cells internalize substances by engulfing them in vesicles formed from the cell membrane. It allows the intake of nutrients and molecules that cannot diffuse through the membrane. Types include phagocytosis for large particles and pinocytosis for fluids and small molecules.

questions.question: ________ are a kind of waste disposal system of the cell.
questions.questionHtml: ________ are a kind of waste disposal system of the cell.
questions.solution: Lysosomes are small, spherical organelles that contain digestive enzymes. They are responsible for breaking down a wide variety of cellular waste products, including worn-out organelles, food particles, and bacteria.

questions.question: Which of the following cell organelles help to keep the cell clean by digesting any foreign material as well as worn-out cell organelles?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following cell organelles help to keep the cell clean by digesting any foreign material as well as worn-out cell organelles?
questions.solution: Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles containing enzymes that break down all types of biological polymers. They help keep the cell clean by digesting foreign materials and worn-out organelles.

questions.question: Which of the following is known as energy currency of the cell?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is known as energy currency of the cell?
questions.solution:
• Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is built up of adenosine and three phosphate groups.
  • It is an energy-carrying molecule found in all living cells.
  • It is known as the energy currency of the cell because all activities inside a living cell need energy which is available in the form of ATP as the immediate source.
  • Adenosine Diphosphate plus terminal phosphate is ATP.

questions.question: Which membrane-bound cell organelle consisting of a small sac-like structure surrounded by single membranes serves as the cell's digestive system, allowing material taken from outside the cell to degrade and digest obsolete components of the cell?
questions.questionHtml: Which membrane-bound cell organelle consisting of a small sac-like structure surrounded by single membranes serves as the cell's digestive system, allowing material taken from outside the cell to degrade and digest obsolete components of the cell?
questions.solution: Lysosomes are small sac-like organelles that act as the cell's digestive system by breaking down unwanted materials. Due to their peculiar function, they are also known as the “suicide bags” of the cell. Lysosomes work as the waste-discarding structures of the cell by processing undesirable materials and degrading them, both from the exterior of the cell and waste constituents inside the cell.

options.html: A plant cell usually contains a large vacuole.

options.html: Generally, all plant cells contain chloroplast.

questions.solution: Mitosis is a type of cell division that occurs in both animal and plant cells. However, plant cells also have the ability to divide by a process called cytoplasmic division, which involves the formation of a cell plate that separates two daughter cells. This process is unique to plant cells and does not occur in animal cells.

questions.question: Which scientist among the following coined the term ‘protoplasm’ for the fluid substance of the cell?
questions.questionHtml: Which scientist among the following coined the term ‘protoplasm’ for the fluid substance of the cell?
questions.solution: The term 'Protoplasm' is given by Purkinje in 1839.It is the living content of a cell that is surrounded by a Plasma Membrane.

questions.question: ______ is the division of the cytoplasm of one eukaryotic cell into two daughter cells.
questions.questionHtml: ______ is the division of the cytoplasm of one eukaryotic cell into two daughter cells.
questions.solution: The correct option is "Cytokinesis".Cytokinesis is the process by which the cytoplasm of a eukaryotic cell divides into two daughter cells after mitosis or meiosis. During cytokinesis, a contractile ring made of actin and myosin filaments forms around the cell, which then contracts and divides the cytoplasm into two parts.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about endoplasmic reticulum? I. It is a large network of membrane-bound tubes and sheets. II. It is similar in structure to the plasma membrane.
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statements is correct about endoplasmic reticulum?

I. It is a large network of membrane-bound tubes and sheets.

II. It is similar in structure to the plasma membrane.
questions.solution: The endoplasmic reticulum is a membrane network dividing the cell into two compartments, with two types, rough and smooth. The latter performs various functions like lipid synthesis, calcium ion storage, detoxification, and glycogenolysis. Both types are structurally similar to the plasma membrane, composed of lipids, proteins, and carbohydrates.

questions.question: Which of the following cell divisions is known as reduction division?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following cell divisions is known as reduction division?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Meiosis.

Key Points

  •  Meiosis:-
    • It is known as reduction division because it reduces the number of chromosomes in a cell by half, resulting in four haploid daughter cells.
    • This process is essential for sexual reproduction as it allows for the formation of gametes with half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell, which then combine during fertilization to form a zygote with a full set of chromosomes.

Additional Information

  • Telophase:-
    • It is a stage in both mitosis and meiosis where the nuclear membrane reforms around the separated chromosomes, but it is not known as reduction division.
  • Prophase:-
    • It is the stage in both mitosis and meiosis where the chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes, but it is not known as reduction division.
  • Mitosis:-
    • It is a type of cell division where a single cell divides into two identical daughter cells, each with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
    • It does not involve a reduction in chromosome number and is not known as reduction division.

questions.question: In cell biology, what is a large double-membraned organelle that is sometimes referred to as the ‘central unit’ of the cell because it contains the chromosomes that bear genetic material?
questions.questionHtml: In cell biology, what is a large double-membraned organelle that is sometimes referred to as the ‘central unit’ of the cell because it contains the chromosomes that bear genetic material?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nucleus.

Key Points

  • The nucleus is a large double-membraned organelle that is sometimes referred to as the ‘central unit’ of the cell because it contains the chromosomes that bear genetic material.
    • It is a membrane-bound organelle found in eukaryotic cells.
    • The main structures making up the nucleus are the nuclear envelope, a double membrane that encloses the entire organelle and isolates its contents from the cellular cytoplasm. 
    • The nuclear matrix (which includes the nuclear lamina), is a network within the nucleus that adds mechanical support, much like the cytoskeleton supports the cell as a whole.
    • It contains DNA arranged in chromosomes.

Additional Information

  • Peroxisome
    • Peroxisomes are small, membrane-enclosed organelles that contain enzymes involved in a variety of metabolic reactions, including several aspects of energy metabolism.
  • Mitochondrion
    • Mitochondria are membrane-bound cell organelles that generate most of the chemical energy needed to power the cell's biochemical reactions.
    • Chemical energy produced by the mitochondria is stored in a small molecule called adenosine triphosphate (ATP).
  • Lysosome
    • Membrane-enclosed organelles contain an array of enzymes capable of breaking down all types of biological polymers—proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, and lipids.

questions.question: In 1955, who published a comprehensive study of small particle constituents of the cytoplasm' (ribosomes) and correctly estimated their physiological importance?
questions.questionHtml: In 1955, who published a comprehensive study of small particle constituents of the cytoplasm' (ribosomes) and correctly estimated their physiological importance?
questions.solution: George Emil Palade, a cell biologist, made groundbreaking discoveries regarding ribosomes, the small particle constituents of the cytoplasm. His work, published in 1955, was crucial for understanding protein synthesis within cells. Utilizing electron microscopy, Palade was the first to visualize ribosomes, highlighting their physiological importance. His significant contributions to cell biology earned him the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1974. Palade's research advanced the field by providing detailed insights into cell structure and function, solidifying his legacy as a pioneer in cellular biology.

questions.question: Read the given statements and select the most appropriate option. i) A white blood cell (WBC) in human blood can change its shape. ii) The shape of amoeba appears irregular.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the given statements and select the most appropriate option.

i) A white blood cell (WBC) in human blood can change its shape.

ii) The shape of amoeba appears irregular.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both statements are correct..

Key Points

  • A white blood cell (WBC) in human blood has the ability to change its shape to move through blood vessels and tissues.
  • This shape-changing ability helps WBCs to perform their function of defending the body against infections.
  • The shape of amoeba is irregular and constantly changes as it moves and feeds.
  • Amoebas move by extending their cell membrane to form pseudopodia (false feet), which helps them to engulf food particles.

Additional Information

  • White Blood Cells (WBCs):
    • WBCs are a crucial part of the immune system and are also known as leukocytes.
    • They are produced in the bone marrow and circulate in the bloodstream and lymphatic system.
    • There are several types of WBCs, including neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, and basophils, each with specific functions in immune response.
  • Amoeba:
    • Amoeba is a single-celled organism belonging to the kingdom Protista.
    • It is known for its ability to change shape due to the formation of pseudopodia.
    • Amoebas are found in various habitats, including freshwater, soil, and as parasites in animals.
  • Pseudopodia:
    • Pseudopodia are temporary projections of the cell membrane and cytoplasm.
    • They are used by amoeboid cells for movement and capturing food through a process called phagocytosis.
  • Phagocytosis:
    • Phagocytosis is the process by which a cell engulfs particles, such as bacteria, other microorganisms, or cellular debris.
    • This process is essential for the immune response and for amoebas to feed.

questions.question: Which cell organelle performs the principal function of packaging materials?
questions.questionHtml: Which cell organelle performs the principal function of packaging materials?
questions.solution: The Golgi apparatus is responsible for packaging materials in the cell. It receives proteins from the endoplasmic reticulum and modifies them before packaging them into vesicles for transportation to their destination. The Golgi also creates complex sugars and form lysosomes. Other organelles, such as the endoplasmic reticulum and lysosomes, have different functions in the cell.

questions.question: Which cell organelle is an overlapping membranous sac with ER-like thickness that helps in processing and packaging protein and lipid molecules, especially stable proteins?
questions.questionHtml: Which cell organelle is an overlapping membranous sac with ER-like thickness that helps in processing and packaging protein and lipid molecules, especially stable proteins?
questions.solution: The Golgi apparatus is a membrane-bound organelle that processes and packages proteins and lipids. It has 5-8 cup-shaped compartments called cisternae, and its main function is packaging and secretion of proteins. It also participates in lipid transport, lysosome formation, and post-translational modification. In plant cells, it synthesizes complex polysaccharides of the cell wall.

questions.question: What are the thin filamentous extensions that the motile bacterial cells have from their cell wall called?
questions.questionHtml: What are the thin filamentous extensions that the motile bacterial cells have from their cell wall called?
questions.solution: The thin filamentous extensions that motile bacterial cells have from their cell wall are called Flagella. These lash-like appendages provide locomotion, allowing bacteria to move toward favorable environments and away from harmful ones. Flagella are composed of the protein flagellin and powered by a rotary engine at their base. Unlike pili and fimbriae, which are primarily used for attachment and not movement, flagella are essential for bacterial motility. Pili are involved in surface attachment and genetic exchange during conjugation, while fimbriae are shorter, more numerous, and aid in attachment to surfaces and other cells.

questions.question: In animal cells, which of the following are the cell’s ‘garbage disposal’?
questions.questionHtml: In animal cells, which of the following are the cell’s ‘garbage disposal’?
questions.solution: The question identifies the cell's "garbage disposal." Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles with digestive enzymes, breaking down cell waste, damaged parts, and invading pathogens. They assist in secretion, apoptosis, and energy metabolism. Unlike lysosomes, vacuoles maintain water balance, the endoplasmic reticulum aids transport and protein folding, and vesicles handle material transport.

questions.solution: A cell's cytoplasm and nucleus are enclosed by the plasma membrane, which acts as a barrier against toxic substances while allowing specific molecules to pass through. Bacterial and plant cells have a cell wall outside the plasma membrane. Biological membranes contain channels and receptors for the movement of nutrients, metabolic products, and waste.

questions.question: Match list I of cell organelles with their functions in list II. List I: (a) Endoplasmic reticulum (b) Vacuoles (c) Golgi apparatus (d) Mitochondria List II: (i) for packaging of materials synthesised near the ER and dispatching them to various targets. (ii) generates ATP. (iii) are storage sacs for solid or liquid contents. (iv) serve as channels for the transport of proteins.
questions.questionHtml:
Match list I of cell organelles with their functions in list II.
List I:
(a) Endoplasmic reticulum
(b) Vacuoles
(c) Golgi apparatus
(d) Mitochondria
List II:
(i) for packaging of materials synthesised near the ER and dispatching them to various targets.
(ii) generates ATP.
(iii) are storage sacs for solid or liquid contents.
(iv) serve as channels for the transport of proteins.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

Key Points

  • Endoplasmic reticulum (a) - (iv): It serves as channels for the transport of proteins.
  • Vacuoles (b) - (iii): These are storage sacs for solid or liquid contents.
  • Golgi apparatus (c) - (i): It is involved in the packaging of materials synthesized near the ER and dispatching them to various targets.
  • Mitochondria (d) - (ii): It generates ATP, which is the energy currency of the cell.

Additional Information

  • Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)
    • It is a network of membranous tubules within the cytoplasm of a eukaryotic cell.
    • There are two types: Rough ER (with ribosomes) and Smooth ER (without ribosomes).
    • Rough ER is involved in protein synthesis, while Smooth ER is involved in lipid synthesis and detoxification processes.
  • Vacuoles
    • They are membrane-bound organelles found in both plant and animal cells.
    • In plant cells, a large central vacuole maintains turgor pressure, which is crucial for maintaining the plant's structural integrity.
    • In animal cells, vacuoles are smaller and often involved in storage and transport.
  • Golgi Apparatus
    • Also known as the Golgi complex or Golgi body.
    • It is responsible for modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or for use within the cell.
    • It consists of a series of flattened, membrane-bound sacs called cisternae.
  • Mitochondria
    • Known as the powerhouse of the cell because they generate most of the cell’s supply of ATP.
    • They are double-membraned organelles with their own DNA, which suggests they were once independent prokaryotic organisms.
    • Mitochondria are involved in other processes like signaling, cellular differentiation, and the control of the cell cycle and cell growth.

questions.question: In the context of movement of cells, exocytosis is the process by which:
questions.questionHtml: In the context of movement of cells, exocytosis is the process by which:

options.text: cells absorb external material by engulfing it with the cell membrane
options.html: cells absorb external material by engulfing it with the cell membrane

options.text: cell death is brought about through a heavily regulated sequence of events
options.html: cell death is brought about through a heavily regulated sequence of events

options.html: cells move waste materials from within the cell into the extracellular fluid

options.html: a cell takes in the fluids along with dissolved small molecules

questions.solution: Exocytosis is a cellular process where materials are moved from within the cell to the extracellular fluid. This involves vesicles fusing with the cell membrane to release their contents outside the cell. Exocytosis is crucial for various functions such as neurotransmitter release, hormone secretion, and waste removal, and requires ATP for energy.

questions.question: The cell wall of spirogyra contains:
questions.questionHtml: The cell wall of spirogyra contains:
questions.solution: The cell wall of Spirogyra contains cellulose, a polysaccharide composed of linear chains of several hundred to many thousands of β(1→4) linked D-glucose units. This cellulose is a primary structural component in green algae and plants, constituting about 30% of their cell walls. Unlike lignin, suberin, and chitin, which are found in different organisms or serve other functions, cellulose provides essential structural support and protection. Spirogyra, a filamentous green algae commonly found in freshwater, is named for its helical chloroplasts and plays a significant role in photosynthesis.

questions.question: Under the electron microscope, which cell organelle is visible as either clusters or single, small dots that float freely in the cytoplasm?
questions.questionHtml: Under the electron microscope, which cell organelle is visible as either clusters or single, small dots that float freely in the cytoplasm?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ribosomes.

Key Points

  • Ribosomes are the cellular structures responsible for protein synthesis.
  • Polyribosomes are clusters of ribosomes may sit on an mRNA and make proteins, each making a strand of polypeptides.
  • These clusters are called polyribosomes. When they are free in the cytoplasm, they are called free polyribosomes (linked by the mRNA). 
  • Ribosomes are the protein factories of the cell.
  • Ribosomes link amino acids together to form polypeptide chains, which are further modified before becoming functional proteins.

Additional Information

  • The Golgi apparatus is responsible for transporting, modifying, and packaging proteins and lipids into vesicles for delivery to targeted destinations.
  • Vesicle is an important term used to describe the appearance of many rashes that typically consist of or begin with tiny-to-small fluid-filled blisters.
  • Pemphigus is classified as one of the blistering diseases.
  • Vesicles are small structures within a cell, consisting of fluid enclosed by a lipid bilayer involved in transport, buoyancy control, and enzyme storage.
  • Peroxisomes are organelles that sequester diverse oxidative reactions and play important roles in metabolism, reactive oxygen species detoxification, and signalling.
  • Oxidative pathways housed in peroxisomes include fatty acid β-oxidation, which contributes to embryogenesis, seedling growth, and stomatal opening.

questions.question: The cytoplasm has ______ such as ribosomes, mitochondria, and Golgi bodies.
questions.questionHtml: The cytoplasm has ______ such as ribosomes, mitochondria, and Golgi bodies.
questions.solution: The correct answer is "organelles". Organelles are specialized structures within a cell that perform specific functions. The term "cytoplasm" refers to the gel-like substance that fills a cell and surrounds the nucleus. It contains various organelles and provides a medium for cellular processes to occur.

questions.question: Which of the following cell organelles is responsible for the storage, modification and packaging of products in vesicles?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following cell organelles is responsible for the storage, modification and packaging of products in vesicles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Golgi apparatus.
Key Points
  • Golgi Apparatus is responsible for storage, modification, and packing of products in vesicles.
  • The Golgi apparatus is also known as the Golgi complex.
  • Golgi Complex was discovered by Camillo Golgi.
  • It is composed of many sac-like structures that are stacked one above another.
  • Function:
    • ​ It packages proteins into membrane-bound vesicles inside the cell before the vesicles are sent to their destination.
    • It is also involved in the storage and modification of contents in the vesicles.
Additional Information
  Basic Function
Plastids Plastids are found in plant cells. They are of two types, chromoplast, and leucoplast. Colorful plastids are called chromoplast and colorless plastids are called leucoplast.  Leucoplasts are responsible for storing food; such as carbohydrates, protein, and lipid. Chromoplasts impart various colors to the plant parts.
Mitochondria  Mitochondria is a capsule-like structure. It is a double membrane structure. Its inner membrane is projected into numerous finger-like structures; called cristae.  Cellular respiration; due to this, mitochondria are also known as the ‘powerhouse of the cell’.
Endoplasmic reticulum The endoplasmic reticulum is a mesh-like structure that is composed of numerous tubes. It extends from the plasma membrane to the nuclear membrane. It serves as the transport channel in the cell. Substances are transported from the cell membrane to the cytoplasm and to the nucleus and vice-versa.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest, double membrane-bound organelles, which contain all the cell’s genetic information?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the largest, double membrane-bound organelles, which contain all the cell’s genetic information?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nucleus.

Key Points

  • The nucleus is the largest double membrane-bound organelle present in eukaryotic cells.
  • It contains the cell's genetic information in the form of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid).
  • The double membrane is called the nuclear envelope, which has nuclear pores to allow the exchange of materials between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
  • The nucleus plays a crucial role in cell division and controls various cellular activities by regulating gene expression.

Additional Information

  • Chromatin: The genetic material in the nucleus exists as chromatin, a complex of DNA and proteins, which condenses to form chromosomes during cell division.
  • Nucleolus: A prominent structure within the nucleus, it is the site of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) synthesis and ribosome assembly.
  • Nuclear Envelope: The double-layered membrane that encloses the nucleus, separating its contents from the cytoplasm.
  • Nuclear Pores: These are large protein complexes that span the nuclear envelope, allowing the transport of molecules between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
  • Functions of the Nucleus: It regulates gene expression, stores genetic information, and coordinates cell activities such as growth, metabolism, and reproduction.

questions.question: What cellular structure is responsible for breaking down and recycling cellular components and molecules?
questions.questionHtml: What cellular structure is responsible for breaking down and recycling cellular components and molecules?
questions.solution: Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles containing hydrolytic enzymes that break down biomolecules like proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, and lipids. They maintain cellular homeostasis by recycling components through autophagy. Lysosomal enzymes function in an acidic environment, maintained by proton pumps. They also aid in immune responses by degrading pathogens in phagolysosomes.

questions.question: In the process of cell division, the formation of phragmoplast between the two daughter nuclei occurs during:
questions.questionHtml: In the process of cell division, the formation of phragmoplast between the two daughter nuclei occurs during:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is cytokinesis

Key Points

  • Cytokinesis is the process during cell division where the cytoplasm of a parental cell is divided between two daughter cells.
  • The formation of the phragmoplast occurs during cytokinesis in plant cells.
  • The phragmoplast is a structure that serves as a scaffold for cell plate assembly and subsequent formation of a new cell wall separating the two daughter cells.
  • It is essential for the successful completion of cell division in plants, ensuring that each daughter cell receives the necessary cellular components.

Additional Information

  • Cell division consists of two main processes: mitosis (karyokinesis) and cytokinesis.
  • Mitosis is the division of the nucleus, whereas cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm.
  • In animal cells, cytokinesis occurs through the formation of a cleavage furrow that pinches the cell into two.
  • In plant cells, the phragmoplast guides the formation of a cell plate, which eventually develops into a separating cell wall.
  • The G0 phase is a resting phase where the cell is not actively preparing to divide.
  • The S phase is the part of the cell cycle where DNA replication occurs.

questions.question: When a cell divides by meiosis it produces ______ new cells.
questions.questionHtml: When a cell divides by meiosis it produces ______ new cells.
questions.solution: When a cell undergoes meiosis, it divides twice to produce four cells, each containing half the original amount of genetic information. This process is crucial for the production of gametes or sex cells. Meiosis takes place in the testes and ovaries of humans, and the end result is four haploid cells. It is different from mitosis, which produces two diploid cells. Oscar Hertwig first described the process of meiosis in the mid-1870s.

questions.question: What is the role of ribosomes of a polysome?
questions.questionHtml: What is the role of ribosomes of a polysome?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Translate the mRNA into proteins.

Key Points

  • Ribosomes of a Polysome 
    • The cellular organelles known as ribosomes are made up of proteins and rRNA.
    • Before they bind to mRNA, they are present free in the cytoplasm.
    • Multiple ribosomes that are joined to the mRNA and contain developing polypeptide chains are known as polysomes.
    • A polysome is made up of all the ribosomes that translate a single mRNA into many polypeptides (Proteins) at once.
    • The coding portion of mRNA, which is transported by multiple ribosomes, forms a polysome.
    • The presence of so much mRNA in cells is due to the ability of multiple ribosomes to participate in an mRNA's function.

Additional Information

  • Prokaryotic, eukaryotic, and membrane-bound polrsomes all have different structures of multiple ribosomes also known as polyribosomes.
  • Bacterial polysomes are found in double-row formations in prokaryotic cells, and ribosomes are in touch with one another within smaller subunits.
  • Planar double row polysomes and densely packed 3D helices, which are similar to that of prokaryotic polysomes, are also present in eukaryotic cells.
  • Polysomal profiling is a method for determining the level of gene expression by monitoring polysome activity. 
  • Translation is stopped using polysomal profiling, and sucrose gradient is then used to separate the resultant cells so that they may be collected by centrifugation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Mitochondria is INCORRECT?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following statements about the Mitochondria is INCORRECT?

options.text: ATP generating chemical reactions get enhanced by the deeply folded surface area of the mitochondria.
options.html: ATP generating chemical reactions get enhanced by the deeply folded surface area of the mitochondria.

options.text: The body uses energy stored in ATP for making new chemical compounds and for mechanical work.
options.html: The body uses energy stored in ATP for making new chemical compounds and for mechanical work.

options.text: Mitochondria are not capable of making their own proteins.
options.html: Mitochondria are not capable of making their own proteins.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mitochondria are not capable of making their own proteins.

Key Points

  • Mitochondria are indeed capable of making their own proteins. They contain their own DNA and ribosomes which allow them to synthesize certain proteins independently.
  • The mitochondrial inner membrane is extensively folded into structures known as cristae, which increase the surface area available for ATP-generating chemical reactions.
  • The energy stored in ATP is used by the body for various processes, including the synthesis of new chemical compounds and mechanical work.
  • Mitochondria have a double-membrane structure. The outer membrane is smooth, while the inner membrane is folded into cristae.

Additional Information

  • Mitochondria
    • Mitochondria are known as the powerhouses of the cell because they generate most of the cell's supply of ATP, used as a source of chemical energy.
    • They are unique in having their own genome, which is similar to bacterial genomes, and they reproduce independently of the cell in which they reside.
    • The double-membrane structure of mitochondria consists of an outer membrane and a highly convoluted inner membrane, the latter being the site of the electron transport chain and ATP synthesis.
    • The inner membrane folds over many times to create layered structures called cristae. The increased surface area of these cristae enhances the mitochondrion's ability to produce ATP.
  • ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)
    • ATP is the energy currency of the cell, providing the energy needed for many biochemical cellular processes including muscle contraction and protein synthesis.
    • It is produced primarily in the mitochondria through a process known as oxidative phosphorylation, which occurs along the inner mitochondrial membrane.
  • Protein Synthesis in Mitochondria
    • Mitochondria have their own ribosomes and DNA, which enable them to produce some of their own proteins independently of the cell's nuclear DNA.
    • The mitochondrial DNA encodes for a small number of proteins essential for the organelle’s function, particularly those involved in the electron transport chain.

questions.question: Which is the major microtubule-organising centre (MTOC) in eukaryotic cells involved in various cellular processes, including sensory reception, locomotion, and embryogenesis?
questions.questionHtml: Which is the major microtubule-organising centre (MTOC) in eukaryotic cells involved in various cellular processes, including sensory reception, locomotion, and embryogenesis?
questions.solution:
The correct option is Centrosome.

Key Points

  • Centrosome is the major microtubule-organising centre (MTOC) in eukaryotic cells involved in various cellular processes, including sensory reception, locomotion, and embryogenesis.
  • MTOC is a structure in eukaryotic cells from which microtubules emerge.
  • Some MTOCs are:
    • Centrosomes (in animals)
    • Basal body (in cilium)
    • Spindle pole body (in yeasts)
  • Cell is the basic unit of life. there are two types of cells:
    • Prokaryotic cells (cells without a nucleus)
    • Eukaryotic cells (cells with a nucleus)
  • Robert Hooke discovered the cell in 1665. Later Anton Van Leeuwenhoek noted that the cells are live. In 1883, Robert Brown, a Scottish botanist, described the nucleus inside the cell.

Additional Information

  • Lysosomes, also known as the Suicide bags of the cell.
  • Plastid is a membrane-bound organelle found in plant cells.
  • Vacuoles, store food, water, and other waste materials in the cell.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding cell membrane? I. The membrane is selectively permeable to some molecules present on either side of it. II. Water may also move across this membrane from lower to higher concentration.
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding cell membrane?

I. The membrane is selectively permeable to some molecules present on either side of it.

II. Water may also move across this membrane from lower to higher concentration.
questions.solution: The cell membrane is a thin, flexible barrier that separates the inside of a cell from its external environment. It is selectively permeable, meaning that it allows some substances to pass through while preventing others from entering or leaving the cell.

questions.question: In animal cells, which membrane-bound cell organelles are generally smaller and help to separate waste products?
questions.questionHtml: In animal cells, which membrane-bound cell organelles are generally smaller and help to separate waste products?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Vacuoles.

Key Points

  • A vacuole is a membrane-bound cell organelle.
  • In animal cells, vacuoles are generally small and help sequester waste products.
  • In plant cells, vacuoles help maintain water balance.
  • Sometimes a single vacuole can take up most of the interior space of the plant cell.

Additional Information

  • Plastids
    • Plastids are double-membrane organelles that are found in the cells of plants and algae.
    • Plastids are responsible for manufacturing and storing food.
  • Cytosols
    • The cytosol is the liquid medium contained within a cell.
    • The cytosol is a component of the cytoplasm.
  • Golgi apparatus
    • The Golgi apparatus, also known as the Golgi complex, Golgi body, or simply the Golgi, is an organelle found in most eukaryotic cells.

questions.question: Which thin flexible barrier separates the internal environment of the cell from the extracellular fluid?
questions.questionHtml: Which thin flexible barrier separates the internal environment of the cell from the extracellular fluid?
questions.solution: The plasma membrane is a thin, flexible barrier that selectively permits hydrophobic and small polar molecules to diffuse through the lipid layer. It inhibits the passage of ions and large polar molecules, but integral proteins facilitate their transport through passive or active transport. Selective permeability filters molecular transport, and membranes can be permeable, or semi-permeable.

questions.question: Which of the following modes of reproduction is carried out by specialised cells that proliferate to make large number of cells?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following modes of reproduction is carried out by specialised cells that proliferate to make large number of cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Regeneration.

  • Regeneration is carried out by specialized cells that proliferate to make a large number of cells.

Key Points

  • Later on these cells differentiate and form different cell types and tissues.
  • These steps occur in an ordered sequence called development.
  • There are four methods of Asexual Reproduction fission, fragmentation, regeneration, and spore formation.
  • In regeneration events like the repair of damaged cells, replacement of affected body parts that are broken and whole organisms can be reconstructed from a small fragment.
  • Examples of the organism in which this process happens are hydra and planaria.

Additional Information 

  • Layering: In this method, practiced in plants, a stem attached to the parent plant branches out to form new plants. Specialized cells are not involved in making a large number of cells here.
  • Fission: This is an asexual mode of reproduction where an organism splits into two or more separate entities. The process does not specifically involve specialised cells proliferating to make many cells.
  • Fragmentation: In fragmentation, the parent organism breaks into fragments, each capable of growing into a new organism. Although this might sound similar to regeneration, specialised cells specifically proliferating to form many cells is not the primary scenario, unlike in regeneration.

questions.question: Which cell organelle is defined as the small round organelle that undergoes oxidation reaction to produce hydrogen peroxide?
questions.questionHtml:
Which cell organelle is defined as the small round organelle that undergoes oxidation reaction to produce hydrogen
peroxide?
questions.solution: Peroxisomes are small, membrane-bound organelles containing enzymes crucial for various metabolic reactions, such as the oxidation of fatty acids and amino acids. They play a significant role in detoxifying harmful substances and in lipid metabolism. During these processes, peroxisomes produce hydrogen peroxide, which is subsequently broken down by the enzyme catalase. In contrast, centrosomes assist in cell division and the formation of cilia and flagella, vacuoles store water and molecules in plant cells, and the nucleus regulates cellular activities and differentiates cells into prokaryotic or eukaryotic based on its presence.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement from the following about mitosis.
questions.questionHtml: Select the INCORRECT statement from the following about mitosis.

options.text: Each cell called mother cell divides to form two identical daughter cells.
options.html: Each cell called mother cell divides to form two identical daughter cells.

options.text: It helps in growth and repair of tissues in organisms.
options.html: It helps in growth and repair of tissues in organisms.

options.text: The daughter cells have half the number of chromosomes as mother cell.
options.html: The daughter cells have half the number of chromosomes as mother cell.

questions.solution: The incorrect statement about mitosis is "The daughter cells have half the number of chromosomes as the mother cell," characteristic of meiosis, not mitosis. Mitosis produces two genetically identical, diploid daughter cells, maintaining chromosome number, essential for growth, tissue repair, and development, unlike meiosis, which forms haploid cells.

questions.question: ________ include/s glycogen, poly-β- hydroxybutyrate granules, sulphur granules and gas vesicles.
questions.questionHtml: ________ include/s glycogen, poly-β- hydroxybutyrate granules, sulphur granules and gas vesicles.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Cytoplasm.

Key Points

  • Cytoplasm include/s glycogen, poly-β- hydroxybutyrate granules, sulphur granules and gas vesicles.
  • The cytoplasm consists of material outside the nucleus in the cell.
  • It consists of the cytoskeleton, ribosomes, and centrosome.
  • The cytoplasm is a gelatin-like, semi-transparent fluid.
  • It contains organelles such as mitochondrion, Golgi apparatus, vacuoles, plastids, cell wall, and the endoplasmic reticulum.

questions.question: Which of the following cell organelles possesses their own DNA and can synthesise protein for their functions?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following cell organelles possesses their own DNA and can synthesise protein for their functions?
questions.solution: Chloroplasts possess their own circular DNA and ribosomes, enabling them to synthesize proteins independently for their functions. Found in plant cells and eukaryotic algae, chloroplasts play a role in photosynthesis. Their double membranes and DNA structure support the endosymbiotic theory of their origin.

questions.question: Choose the correct sequence for central dogma.
questions.questionHtml: Choose the correct sequence for central dogma.

options.text: Protein translation, DNA Replication, m-RNA transcription
options.html: Protein translation, DNA Replication, m-RNA transcription

options.text: DNA Replication, m-RNA transcription, Protein translation
options.html: DNA Replication, m-RNA transcription, Protein translation

options.text: m-RNA transcription, Protein translation, DNA Replication
options.html: m-RNA transcription, Protein translation, DNA Replication

options.text: m-RNA transcription, DNA Replication, Protein translation
options.html: m-RNA transcription, DNA Replication, Protein translation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is DNA Replication, mRNA transcription, Protein translation .

Key Points

  • The process by which DNA is copied to RNA is called transcription, and that by which RNA is used to produce proteins is called translation.
  • The major steps of transcription are initiation, promoter clearance, elongation, and termination.
  • Essentially, what happens during transcription is that an mRNA “copies down” the instructions for making a protein from DNA.
  • DNA replication is the process by which the genome's DNA is copied in cells.
  • The process of translation can be seen as the decoding of instructions for making proteins, involving mRNA in transcription as well as tRNA.

Additional Information

  • Deoxyribonucleic acid (abbreviated DNA) is the molecule that carries genetic information for the development and functioning of an organism.
  • Ribonucleic acid (abbreviated RNA) is a nucleic acid present in all living cells that has structural similarities to DNA.
  • Proteins are made up of hundreds or thousands of smaller units called amino acids, which are attached to one another in long chains.
  • Proteins are 20 different types of amino acids that can be combined to make a protein.

questions.question: A Eukaryotic cell has membrane bound organelles, including a nucleus, which allow cellular processes to be carried out in _________
questions.questionHtml: A Eukaryotic cell has membrane bound organelles, including a nucleus, which allow cellular processes to be carried out in _________
questions.solution: The correct answer is Isolation. Eukaryotic cells contain collections of proteins that function as a unit called organelles. Some of these organelles are surrounded by a membrane similar in structure to the cell membrane but with a different composition of protein and phospholipid.

questions.question: Which cytologist demonstrated the role of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) in protein processing and sorting in a variety of cells in the 1960s?
questions.questionHtml: Which cytologist demonstrated the role of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) in protein processing and sorting in a variety of cells in the 1960s?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is George E Palade.

Key Points 
  • George E Palade:-
    • He was a Romanian-American cell biologist who demonstrated the role of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) in protein processing and sorting in the 1960s.
    • Palade's discovery led to the understanding of how proteins are made, modified, and transported within cells.
    • He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1974 for his work on the structure and function of cells.
    • Palade's research also paved the way for further studies on the mechanisms of protein synthesis and secretion, as well as the development of treatments for diseases related to protein misfolding and trafficking.

questions.question: By what name are the flat membrane-enclosed sacs present in the Golgi apparatus known?
questions.questionHtml: By what name are the flat membrane-enclosed sacs present in the Golgi apparatus known?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Cisternae

Key Points

  • Cisternae are the flat, membrane-enclosed sacs that are a characteristic feature of the Golgi apparatus.
  • The Golgi apparatus is an essential cellular organelle involved in the modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins and lipids.
  • Each stack of cisternae has a distinct polarity with a cis face (receiving side) and a trans face (shipping side).
  • The cisternae play a crucial role in the transport and processing of cellular materials.

Additional Information

  • Lamellae are thin layers, plates, or discs in various structures, but not specific to the Golgi apparatus.
  • Cristae are the folds in the inner membrane of mitochondria, increasing the surface area for ATP production.
  • Stroma refers to the fluid-filled space in chloroplasts surrounding the thylakoid membranes, involved in the synthesis of organic molecules.

questions.question: In 1873, who published the first photograph of nerve tissue stained with the black reaction technique, describing a whole nerve cell?
questions.questionHtml: In 1873, who published the first photograph of nerve tissue stained with the black reaction technique, describing a whole nerve cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Camillo Golgi.

Key Points

  • Camillo Golgi developed the black reaction technique (also known as Golgi's method) in 1873, which was a major advancement in neuroanatomy.
  • This staining technique made it possible to visualize the detailed structure and organization of nerve cells and their intricate networks.
  • The black reaction involves using silver chromate to stain a few cells in their entirety, allowing for the observation of individual neurons against a transparent background.
  • This method was instrumental in establishing the neuron doctrine, which states that the neuron is the basic structural and functional unit of the nervous system.
  • Golgi shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1906 with Santiago Ramón y Cajal for their work on the structure of the nervous system.

Additional Information

  • The Golgi apparatus, an important cellular organelle involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles, was also discovered by Camillo Golgi.
  • Golgi's contributions to cell biology and neuroscience are foundational, with the Golgi method continuing to influence neuroscientific research well into the 20th century and beyond.
  • His work laid the groundwork for understanding the complex connectivity and functions of the nervous system, influencing both basic science and clinical approaches to neurological diseases.
  • The Golgi method's ability to selectively stain neurons is still appreciated for its utility in highlighting the intricate details of cell morphology and connectivity.

questions.question: Antibiotics are NOT effective on a virus as a virus lacks _____.
questions.questionHtml: Antibiotics are NOT effective on a virus as a virus lacks _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is cell wall.

Key Points

  •  Antibiotics are not effective on a virus as it lacks a cell wall.
  • How antibiotics work
    • They are used to treat infections caused by bacteria.
    • There are two types of antibiotics that work to stop bacterial infections.
    • Some slow down the growth of bacteria and damage their ability to reproduce and spread.
    • While others kill the bacteria by destroying the bacteria cell walls. The choice of antibiotic depends on the type of bacteria.

Additional Information

  • Viruses are different from bacteria; they have a different structure and a different way of surviving. Viruses don’t have cell walls that can be attacked by antibiotics.​

Important Points

  • Antibiotics were discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928.

questions.question: What is the length of a bacterial cell?
questions.questionHtml: What is the length of a bacterial cell?
questions.solution: Bacteria are diverse, single-celled prokaryotes ranging in size from 3 to 5 µm. They come in various shapes, including cocci (spherical), bacilli (rod-shaped), and spirilla (spiral-shaped). Bacteria can reproduce rapidly through binary fission and can exchange genetic material via transformation, transduction, and conjugation. They play critical roles in ecosystems, including nutrient cycling, nitrogen fixation, and supporting human health through the gut microbiome.

questions.question: On which of the following component of chloroplast is chlorophyll arranged?
questions.questionHtml: On which of the following component of chloroplast is chlorophyll arranged?
questions.solution: Chlorophyll is primarily arranged in the thylakoids of the chloroplast, which are membrane-bound compartments inside chloroplasts and cyanobacteria. Thylakoids are the site of the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis and contain chlorophyll and other pigments that capture light energy. The chloroplast is an organelle found in plant cells and eukaryotic algae that conduct photosynthesis. The stroma, which surrounds the thylakoids, is involved in the synthesis of organic molecules from carbon dioxide and water. The matrix refers to the internal structure of mitochondria, and the cell membrane separates the interior of all cells from the outside environment.
